@saltypeanuts thanks for reporting this and for using Numba. Another simplified jit loop that has caused crashes while wrapped:


```
@jit(nopython = True)
def test_loop(array1, array2):
    out = np.zeros(len(array1))
    for i in range(1, len(array1)):
        out[i] = (array1[i] - array2[i]) / (array1[i-1] - array2[i-1])
    return out
```

Tested across three machines. Wrapping the functions has a 100% failure rate over ~50 iterations.

Running without them wrapped has a ~54% failure rate (7 of 13 attempts)

Figured out what's happening, but I can't reproduce it.

The dead kernel is being caused by an out of bounds loop that isn't correctly erroring out. When I fixed the out of bounds loop, I've had 100% run success. The dead kernel happened ~40% of the time when nested twice (ntrials = 74) and 100% when nested 3 times.

```
series = pd.Series([0,1,2,3,4,5,6])
def first_test_loop(series):
    series = second_test_loop(series.values)
    return series

@jit(nopython = True)        
def second_test_loop(array):      
    for i in range(0, len(array)+1):
        array[i] = 5*array[i]
    return(array)
        
series = first_test_loop(series)
```
Incorrectly returns: [ 0  5 10 15 20 25 30]

When it should error out

```
series = pd.Series([0,1,2,3,4,5,6])
array = series.values
out = second_test_loop(array)
print(out)

```

Incorrectly returns: [ 0  5 10 15 20 25 30]
